description: Friction overlap root cause investigation and partial fix (Nov 21 instruction item 3)

root_cause.mechanism: Plate friction in hold steps changes the held sphere horizontal velocity. Between hold steps, the sphere drifts at this new velocity toward touching neighbours. The drift per step (about 2.3e-7 diameters) exceeds the overlap tolerance (2e-8) after one step.
root_cause.code_path: granular/edmd.py hold_cluster_step, lines 1097-1113: friction impulse S[a,SVX] += ptx, S[a,SVY] += pty
root_cause.previous_workaround: Widened tolerance htol=1e-3 in re-prediction (line 1210), which tolerated growing overlaps instead of preventing them
root_cause.traced_pair: Spheres 80 and 81 in a 2D Gamma 3.5, f*0.3, depth 10, N=100 run

fix_attempted.name: _friction_gap_limit
fix_attempted.approach: After computing each friction impulse, scan all particles. For each non-cluster neighbour within gap < 1e-4, compute the closing rate from the friction velocity change and scale the impulse to keep the gap non-negative (using half the gap as the limit).
fix_attempted.result: Partial success. The fix delays overlap failures from cycle 1 to cycle 10-11 at the test condition. The remaining failures may be from cluster members (excluded from the scan) or the z-component of wall friction (not fully checked). The gap limiter correctly limits plate friction for isolated held-sphere/non-held-neighbour pairs.
fix_attempted.status: partial — friction remains off by default until complete

tests_run.result: 50 cycles clean — confirming the tolerance alone is not the issue
